newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank to help ailing Finance One.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank to help ailing Finance One.

text.p: Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Sunday the Bank of Thailand was ready to help bail out cash-strapped finance firm, Finance One Plc, following the collapse of its planned merger with a bank.
"The central bank via its rehabilitation fund is ready to buy Finance One's new shares if existing shareholders don't want to take those shares," Amnuay told reporters.

The central bank on Friday ordered ailing Finance One to raise its capital by 8.28 billion baht ($318 million) through a two-for-one rights issue at 7.50 baht a share after its planned merger with medium-sized Thai Danu Bank Plc collapsed last week.
Finance One and Thai Danu on Friday closed two months of merger talks with announcements that they would not link up because of complicated legal and tax issues.
"The rehalibitation fund would also help improve the management and administration of Finance One," Amnuay said.
Despite the failure to merge with other financial institutions, Finance One's financial status remained viable as the company still had high retained earnings and net capital, he added.
